note: Countries whose surname data was sought. Those still not obtained are in `refused`, with what was actually tried; those since obtained are in `resolved`, with how. A gap somebody can see is worth more than a gap they cannot, and without this file the next person spends the same afternoon finding the same walls. A «not found» verdict is weaker than a «refused» one: it means this project looked and did not find, not that the data is absent. Both are worth writing down and they are not the same claim. Italy was the weakest entry here — «not found» — and retrying it is what closed it, which is the argument for keeping this file honest about the difference. TWO CORRECTIONS ON 22 SEPTEMBER, BOTH THE SAME MISTAKE. A reader asked why Croatia was blank and sent the Bureau of Statistics' own name application, which answers. Checking the other six the same way — the institution's website, not its API — closed Denmark outright and rewrote Sweden and Finland. Four of these entries had searched an API exhaustively and concluded about an organisation. That is the failure this file now exists to catch, and it was not caught by this project.

refused.name: Belgium
tried: statbel.fgov.be/en/open-data — the full open-data catalogue searched for name/nom/naam
statbel.fgov.be/en/open-data?category=51 — the population open-data category itself, read and searched for surname / nom de famille / familienaam / achternaam: not one dataset
refused.why: RECHECKED 22 September against the website, in the pass that corrected Croatia and closed Denmark, and Belgium is the one that did not move. Statbel publishes first names in exhaustive detail — by year, region and sex — and the population open-data category, read directly rather than searched through an API, contains no surname dataset in any of the three languages it publishes in. The gap is in what Belgium chooses to publish, not in what it holds, and no interactive lookup stands behind it either.

refused.name: Czechia
tried: mvcr.cz/clanek/cetnost-jmen-a-prijmeni.aspx — the page loads and is headed «Archiv», with no file of any kind left on it
no surname table in the Czech Statistical Office's own catalogue
mvcr.cz/clanek/cetnost-jmen-a-prijmeni — followed the redirect to mv.gov.cz, which 404s
data.gov.cz SPARQL — the national open data catalogue, searched for «příjmení»
one record: «Četnost příjmení v ČR», IRI data.gov.cz/zdroj/podněty-na-data-k-otevření/R23
refused.verdict: formally requested, and formally refused in law
refused.why: RETRIED 21 September against the national catalogue rather than the old ministry page, and this is a better answer than the one this file had. The only record of Czech surname frequency in data.gov.cz is not a dataset at all — it sits in the register of REQUESTS for data to be opened (podněty na data k otevření, R23, filed 7 May 2024, publisher the Ministry of the Interior). Its status is «NelzePublikovat» — cannot be published — and it carries the flag existuje-překážka-dle-z. 106/1999 Sb., an obstacle under the Czech Act on Free Access to Information. So somebody asked for exactly this, through the proper channel, and the answer was a legal no. That is not a dead link or a page that moved; it is a decision, and it is the strongest evidence in this file. NOT RECHECKED 22 September, deliberately, while the other five were. The answer here is not an endpoint that might have moved — it is a decision recorded in the national catalogue under the Act on Free Access to Information. Re-fetching a URL would not change it, and pretending to have looked again would make this file less honest, not more current.

refused.name: Finland
tried: pxdata.stat.fi StatFin — all 135 subject folders, none name-related
avoindata.fi — HTTP 403 to every request
avoindata.fi CKAN — 403 to an identified crawler
pxdata.stat.fi PxWeb — answers, and holds no names
dvv.fi/en/name-service — the DVV's own page, which offers an interactive lookup and points at avoindata.fi for the dataset
nimipalvelu.dvv.fi — the lookup itself, which answers 200 to a plain request and is a JavaScript application with no documented API
refused.verdict: a working lookup for humans; the file is behind the gate
refused.why: RECHECKED 22 September against the DVV's website rather than the open-data portal. Statistics Finland has no names and never did — they belong to the DVV — and the DVV does publish: nimipalvelu.dvv.fi answers, and gives the number of people carrying any forename or surname in the Population Information System. It is a JavaScript application, and the DVV's own page sends anyone wanting the DATA to avoindata.fi, which answers 403 to an identified agent. Guessing at the application's private endpoints until one answered was considered and rejected: it is the same act as climbing the gate, done less honestly. THIS ATLAS DOES NOT CLIMB BOT GATES, and it does not go round the back of them either. Finland stays refused until a human downloads the avoindata file or the gate lifts — and unlike before, we now know exactly which file that is.

refused.name: Croatia
tried: podaci.dzs.hr CKAN package_search for «prezimena» — no parseable response
data.gov.hr CKAN package_search for «prezimena» — answers 200 but not JSON
podaci.dzs.hr CKAN — 404
opendata.dzs.hr — no answer
web.dzs.hr/PXWeb/api/v1 — the whole PxWeb tree walked two levels deep, looking for ime/prezime/name in every folder
web.dzs.hr/app/imena/default_en.aspx — DZS's own «Names and surnames» application, which ANSWERS: HORVAT 21,618, KOVAČEVIĆ 15,160, NOVAK 10,794, from the 2011 Population Census
refused.verdict: queryable, not enumerable — and this file was wrong about it
refused.why: CORRECTED 22 September, and the correction matters more than the entry. This file said «the API answers now, and holds no names», which was a true statement about the wrong thing: the DZS PxWeb API really does have no surname table, and walking it exhaustively proved only that the data is not THERE. It is at web.dzs.hr/app/imena — the Bureau's own «Names and surnames» application, 2011 census, one name at a time behind an ASP.NET form, with a confidentiality floor of 10. It was found by a reader who simply looked at the statistics office's website, which this project had stopped doing the moment its API said no. A negative from one endpoint is not a negative from an institution, and «I searched the machine-readable catalogue» is not «Croatia does not publish this». It stays in this file because it is still not a corpus. There is no listing endpoint: the application will tell you about a surname you already have and will not tell you which surnames exist, so no amount of polite querying produces the table Slovenia and Italy publish. Brute-forcing the alphabet at a government service to synthesise a list it declines to publish would be taking by volume what it offers by question, and this atlas does not do that. What it does instead is scripts/harvest-croatia-surnames.py: ask only about the 466 surnames the atlas already attests in archives whose declared country is Croatia, and write the answers to data/frequencies/hr.json marked `enumerable: false`. Croatia is therefore no longer a blank — it is a partial, honestly bounded one. Closing it properly needs the table, and the table is not published.

refused.name: Netherlands
tried: opendata.cbs.nl catalogue search — no surname table
cbgfamilienamen.nl (Meertens familienamenbank) — HTTP 403
cbgfamilienamen.nl/nfb/ — still 403
nfb.meertens.knaw.nl — does not answer at all
refused.why: CBS publishes no surname frequencies. The real Dutch source is the Meertens Nederlandse Familienamenbank, which is a research database rather than open government data. RECHECKED 22 September in the pass that corrected Croatia and closed Denmark: cbgfamilienamen.nl still answers 403 and the Meertens host does not answer at all. This one is unchanged and does not need a cleverer harvester — it needs an email. The letter is written and waiting at docs/letter-meertens.md. Of the five countries left, the Netherlands and Finland are the only two obtainable at all, and both need a human rather than a script.

refused.name: Sweden
tried: api.scb.se BE0001 «Namnstatistik» — the folder is listed and its two sub-folders, BE0001D and BE0001G, both answer 400 Bad Request
api.scb.se/OV0104/v1/doris/en/ssd/BE/BE0001 — the two name folders found, then opened
api.scb.se/OV0104/v1/doris/en/ssd/BE/BE0001 — 200, lists BE0001D and BE0001G
api.scb.se/OV0104/v1/doris/en/ssd/BE/BE0001/BE0001G — 400
api.scb.se/OV0104/v1/doris/sv/ssd/BE/BE0001/BE0001G — 400, so it is not a language problem
scb.se/namnstatistik — the statistics page itself, not the database
scb.se Namnsök — a working lookup covering every surname with at least ten bearers among the registered population
skatteverket.se — where SCB now sends people, and also a search
refused.verdict: a lookup and a top-100 table; the full list is not published
refused.why: RECHECKED 22 September against the website rather than the database, after the same check corrected Croatia and closed Denmark. The old verdict — «the tables are retired, not withheld» — was right about PxWeb and incomplete about Sweden. SCB stopped producing name statistics altogether in 2024 and now refers enquirers to Skatteverket. What remains on scb.se is a top-100 surnames table and Namnsök, a working public lookup over every surname with at least ten bearers. So Sweden is Croatia's shape, not Denmark's: the data exists and is answerable one name at a time, and no complete list is published by anybody. A hundred names is not a register and this atlas will not present it as one.

resolved.name: Italy
tried: esploradati.istat.it SDMX dataflow list — no parseable response to a documented Accept header
istat.it — responds, but publishes no surname frequency series that this probe could find
resolved.verdict: closed, by the comuni rather than the state
resolved.why: ISTAT does not appear to publish surname frequencies. What circulates for Italy is derived from telephone directories by commercial sites, which is neither open nor redistributable. Recorded as NOT FOUND rather than as absent — a human who knows ISTAT may know better, and this is three archives' core ground.
resolved.how: ISTAT publishes no national surname table. 63 Italian comuni publish their own residents' surnames as open data and dati.gov.it indexes them — 27,005 surnames, 1,398,684 people, now in data/frequencies/it.json. It counts the residents of those comuni and nobody else, which is stated on the data and must stay stated: it is evidence that a name is borne in Italy and roughly where, never how common it is in Italy. For genealogy that is the more useful grain anyway — which comune a name sits in is the question a national total cannot answer.

resolved.name: Denmark
tried: api.statbank.dk — all 2,308 tables listed and searched for navn/fornavn/efternavn: none
dst.dk/da/Statistik/emner/borgere/navne — the page exists and offers «hvor mange hedder», an interactive lookup for one name at a time
api.statbank.dk/v1/tables — the COMPLETE table list, 531 KB, searched for 'navn'
sprogteknologi.dk — Digitaliseringsstyrelsen's republication of Danmarks Statistik's own name lists, CC BY 4.0: navne_registreret_i_danmark_2020.zip
resolved.verdict: CLOSED — it was on the website all along, not in the bank
resolved.why: RESOLVED 22 September, and this entry is kept in full because being wrong here was instructive. The refusal was not lazy: all 2,308 tables in api.statbank.dk were downloaded and searched for «navn», twice, and the finding — not one table mentions it — was true. It was also useless, because Denmark does not put its name statistics in the statistics bank. It puts them on its website. The same mistake as Croatia, found on the same afternoon, by the same method: a reader looked at the institution instead of its API. This project had built a habit of asking machines and concluding about organisations. What is published, under CC BY 4.0, is every surname borne by three or more people in Denmark as of January 2020 — 294,496 of them, harvested by scripts/harvest-denmark-surnames.py. AND NO COUNTS AT ALL: Denmark says which surnames exist and declines to say how many carry each, so the file is marked `counted: false` and its rows must never be summed. A figure for one name comes from «Hvor mange hedder...?», which is Denmark's version of the Croatian lookup. HELD BACK FOR AN HOUR, WRONGLY. 294,496 names is about 79 MB of surname shards, and this project nearly deferred shipping them against GitHub Pages' 1,024 MB — by measuring raw bytes, which is the exact mistake worklist row 25 was written to stop. The deploy's own report says the published artifact is 385 MB stored from 2,142 MB of files. Denmark costs about 18 MB of that. Measure the unit the limit is in.
